rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣfāʾ means to choose someone or something exclusively; Arabian idolaters treated angels as God's daughters and worshipped them as intercessors with their father.
rows.anchor: The Idolaters of Arabia regarded angels to be the daughters of God and would worship them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their claim grave means it compounds foolishness: they assign God what they dislike for themselves, lowering Him beneath their own status.
rows.anchor: they choose for God what they do not like for their own selves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic verb means to circulate; here it describes explaining a reality in varied styles and ways.
rows.anchor: Here it means to explain the reality in different styles and multiple ways.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who are not stubborn can understand repeated clarification, while the belligerent grow more averse because they see it as defeat and humiliation.
rows.anchor: people who are stubborn and belligerent and are not willing to accept the truth, become more averse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabian idolaters pictured God as a supreme king and other deities as subordinate partners who mediated nearness; the verse refutes that conception.
rows.anchor: By analogy to the kings and kingdoms of this world, the Idolaters of Arabia regarded God to be the supreme deity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had partners, they would contend for power and overthrow Him; the orderly paths of sun and earth show otherwise, as 21:22 says creation would be disrupted if there were other gods.
rows.anchor: if God also had partners, why would they have sat peacefully? Why would they have not forced their way to defeat the supreme God?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is transcendent above the foolish conjectures people make about Him; these speculations do not accord with His higher attributes.
rows.anchor: God is beyond these foolish conjectures they make about Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ absolves God of negative traits; when joined with praise, it affirms His higher attributes.
rows.anchor: The real meaning of ﺗﺴﺒﻴﺢis to absolve someone of negative traits.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants humans limited freedom, which they misuse by making whatever accusations against Him they wish.
rows.anchor: God has blessed people with the freedom to exercise their will in a certain sphere.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures between the heavens and earth glorify God, even though people do not understand their glorification.
rows.anchor: the seven heavens and the earth and all the creatures found between them all glorify God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ascription of partners is so grave that the heavens would have fallen upon them; God's benevolence and forgiveness nevertheless grant them respite despite their misdeeds.
rows.anchor: Such is the grave nature of their ascribing partners to God that the heavens would have fallen on them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for hearing means making sarcastic remarks; al-Furqān 25:8–9 provides parallels.
rows.anchor: For parallels, readers can look up verses 8-9 of Sūrah al-Furqān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to find a sound objection to the Prophet and Qur'an, they vent frustration by calling him a soothsayer, madman, or magician; he should be patient.
rows.anchor: they do not find any way to raise objections on the Prophet (sws) and the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse presents their view that resurrection after becoming bones and fragments is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: This verse cites their view about the far-fetched nature of the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question about who could restore them is rhetorical, already answered negatively in their minds; the Qur'an answers that the one who first created them can recreate them from nothing without difficulty.
rows.anchor: when God easily created them from nothingness the first time, how could He face any difficulty in recreating them?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will shake their heads sarcastically and ask when resurrection will occur; only God knows its time, and its certainty does not depend on whether people know when it will come.
rows.anchor: only God knows about this time. Not even a prophet is privy to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not knowing when death will arrive does not make death unreal; someone who denies it for that reason is foolish, just as with resurrection.
rows.anchor: a person who denies death merely because its time of arrival is not known must be regarded as foolish.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh will see truths fully unveiled at Judgment and think they had only slept briefly; each person who dies will feel Judgment is near and retain no memory of the Barzakh interval.
rows.anchor: They will think that they had just slept a while ago and now woken up.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because opponents mock and mistreat the Prophet and Muslims, believers must answer only with what is better and communicate truth without replying to foolish taunts; Satan seeks to sow dissension.
rows.anchor: They should only try to communicate to them what is the truth and correct

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This guidance parallels the instruction in 16:125 to preach with wisdom, kind exhortation, and proper debate, and the related discussion in 7:198–201.
rows.anchor: Precisely the same guidance is given to them in the same background in S ūrah al-Naḥl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's and believers' duty is to convey truth, not force belief; God knows who merits mercy for guidance and punishment for straying, and holds the Prophet accountable only for his duty to communicate.
rows.anchor: Their only responsibility is to communicate the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To prevent rivalry and disorder caused by exaggerating one's leaders, Muslims should recognize that prophetic superiority is relative, not absolute, and acknowledge each prophet's distinctive gifts, including those of Moses, Jesus, David, and Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: As for the superiority of prophets, it is relative and not absolute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Psalms' distinctive feature is that they are the only versified divine book and consist entirely of hymns and holy glorification.
rows.anchor: the only versified divine book and entirely composed of hymns and holy glorification.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the parenthetical admonition in 17:53–55, the discourse returns to 17:51–52: those who demand punishment should invoke their alleged partners, who cannot avert or delay it.
rows.anchor: Now the discourse once again connects back to verses 51-52.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings whom the idolaters invoke are angels; they themselves seek closeness to their Lord, hope for mercy, and fear His punishment.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the angels.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 58–60 explain God's established practice concerning torment signs, answering why He does not send a demanded sign simply because people ask for one; the earlier demand appears in 17:11.
rows.anchor: the established practice of God about it is explained.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term for a town refers to its central and main city, where its leaders and nobles reside.
rows.anchor: refers to the central and main cities where their leadership and nobles reside.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers the Quraysh's demand for a punishment sign and invokes God's established practice in 17:16: a people that rejects its messenger after conclusive communication receives respite and is then destroyed, as decreed in God's register.
rows.anchor: a messenger is the final means of conclusive communication of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God withholds demanded signs because earlier peoples rejected them instead of heeding their warning, thereby opening the way to punishment; the Thamūd's she-camel illustrates this.
rows.anchor: previous nations because of their wretchedness instead of paying heed to such signs ended up rejecting them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi implies an omitted verb such as ‘they denied’: the Thamūd wronged themselves by denying the she-camel sign.
rows.anchor: they were unjust to their souls and denied the sign of the she-camel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning signs are twisted to fit the obdurate people's wishes; only the actual punishment convinces them, when belief is already immaterial.
rows.anchor: What can only convince them is the punishment itself. However, once it arrives, being convinced will become immaterial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that God had surrounded the Prophet's people shows the Quraysh being gradually encircled as Islam spread; the cited sign describes God advancing toward Makkah while diminishing the disbelievers' power.
rows.anchor: It was as if the people of Makkah were gradually being surrounded by Islam.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stubborn Quraysh mocked God's warning that He had surrounded them instead of taking heed.
rows.anchor: they mocked and derided him instead of taking heed from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further victory that the addressees could not yet achieve was nevertheless within God's grasp, as 48:21 predicts.
rows.anchor: And another victory also on which you do not have power as yet. However, God has it in His grasp.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream refers to the Ascension at the beginning of the sūrah, a warning to Quraysh and Israelites that custodianship of the two houses of God would pass from corrupt custodians to Muḥammad and his followers; their mockery made it a trial.
rows.anchor: refers to the ascension mentioned at the beginning of this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed tree is zaqqūm in Hell (44:43); the starving inhabitants eat it and then drink boiling water, while it is the opposite of a blessed tree, offering no shade or fruit and consisting of thorns, poison, and sourness.
rows.anchor: They refer to the zaqqūm tree about which the Qur’ ān (44:43) has stated that it will be in Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh mocked the description of zaqqūm through worldly analogy, asking how a tree could survive in fire and water coexist with it.
rows.anchor: How can a tree survive in fire? How can water and fire co-exist?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People whose perception is distorted will not learn from a sign of punishment and will invent excuses for it.
rows.anchor: people whose minds have become so distorted that what is straight appears twisted to them should not be expected to believe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who misread warnings will only be convinced by actual punishment, after which belief or disbelief no longer matters.
rows.anchor: They will only be convinced if they see the actual punishment – after which belief or disbelief becomes immaterial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage identifies the source of the people's arrogance: ingratitude for God's favors and following Satan, thereby confirming Satan's claim about Adam's progeny.
rows.anchor: they have become arrogant instead of being grateful to Him.
